_meta.indication: KALBITOR is a plasma kallikrein inhibitor indicated for treatment of acute attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in patients 16 years of age and older.
_meta.receipt_date: May 31, 2009 (Complete Response to previous action); original BLA submitted September 23, 2008.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm, multi-center study; patients presenting within 8 hours of an acute moderate to severe attack randomized 1:1 to a single dose of ecallantide 30 mg SC or placebo.
pivotal_trials.population: HAE patients presenting within 8 hours of recognition of an acute attack with symptom complexes assessed as moderate or severe.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was the Treatment Outcome Score (TOS) at 4 hours post-dose.
pivotal_trials.result: Mean TOS at 4 hrs: ecallantide 49.5 vs placebo 18.5, difference 31.0 (p=0.037) in the ITT-as-treated population; the difference was not significant (p=0.100) in the ITT-as-randomized population.

pivotal_trials.design: Randomized, double-blind, placebo-controlled, parallel-arm, multi-center study conducted similarly to EDEMA3, under a Special Protocol Agreement; conducted in North America.
pivotal_trials.population: HAE patients presenting during an acute moderate to severe attack, enrolled similarly to EDEMA3.
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Primary efficacy endpoint was change of Mean Symptom Complex Severity (MSCS) score at 4 hours post-dose from baseline.
pivotal_trials.result: Mean change from baseline in MSCS at 4 hrs: ecallantide -0.81 vs placebo -0.37, difference -0.44 (p=0.01); secondary endpoint TOS at 4 hrs difference 45.3 (p=0.003).

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions in 255 HAE patients were headache (16.1%), nausea (12.9%), fatigue (11.8%), diarrhea (10.6%), upper respiratory tract infection (8.2%) and injection site reactions (7.4%). The most serious risk is anaphylaxis, reported in 3.9% of patients.
target_moa: Ecallantide is a potent, selective, reversible inhibitor of plasma kallikrein; by directly inhibiting plasma kallikrein it reduces the conversion of HMW kininogen to bradykinin, thereby treating acute HAE attacks.
modality: Peptide/protein – a recombinant 60 amino acid protein identified by phage display from human tissue factor pathway inhibitor (TFPI).

boxed_warning.content: WARNING: ANAPHYLAXIS – Anaphylaxis has been reported after administration of KALBITOR; because of the risk of anaphylaxis, KALBITOR should only be administered by a healthcare professional with appropriate medical support to manage anaphylaxis and hereditary angioedema.

rems.type: A REMS consisting of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments was approved at approval.

advisory_committee.vote: A Pulmonary Allergy Drugs Advisory Committee met February 4, 2009; voting favored that efficacy was sufficient in patients 18 and older (8 Yes, 4 No, 1 Abstain) but not in those under 18 (3 Yes, 10 No), and on recommendation for approval the committee was split (6 Yes, 5 No, 2 Abstain).

HAE is estimated to affect 1 in 10,000 to 50,000 individuals worldwide and is categorized as an orphan disease in the US.

basis.text: The application was reviewed under Priority review.

summary.text: Ecallantide received orphan drug designation for HAE and was reviewed under Priority review; an earlier fast track request was denied. The original BLA was not approved in the first cycle due to efficacy, safety, and product quality concerns, and was approved after a Complete Response, with a REMS (Medication Guide and communication plan) required for the risk of anaphylaxis.

citations.quote: On February 4, 2003, orphan drug designation was granted.

The application was not approved in the previous review cycle because efficacy and safety was not demonstrated for the proposed age range, particularly ages 10 years to 18 years, and the requirements for a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) to mitigate the risk of anaphylaxis had not been agreed upon. In addition, there were outstanding product quality related issues.

Your proposed REMS, submitted on December 1, 2009, and appended to this letter, is approved. The REMS consists of a Medication Guide, a communication plan, and a timetable for submission of assessments of the REMS.

requirement.text: A long-term, observational safety study in HAE patients to evaluate hypersensitivity, immunogenicity, and coagulation disorders.

citations.quote: - A long-term, observational safety study with Kalbitor (ecallantide) in patients with hereditary angioedema to evaluate hypersensitivity, immunogenicity, and coagulation disorders. The study should include the following objectives: 1) identify predictive risk factors and develop effective screening tools to mitigate the risk of hypersensitivity and anaphylaxis; 2) correlate antibody levels with adverse events and lack of efficacy; and 3) evaluate the risk of hypercoagulability and hypocoagulability.

date.text: Complete Response submitted May 31, 2009 to the previous (non-approval) action on the original BLA.

citations.quote: Dyax Corp submitted a complete response on May 31, 2009, to the previous action on the original biologics license application (BLA) for use of ecallantide for the treatment of acute attacks of hereditary angioedema (HAE) in patients 10 years of age and older. The proposed dose is 30 mg by subcutaneous (SC) injection. The application was not approved in the previous review cycle because efficacy and safety was not demonstrated for the proposed age range, particularly ages 10 years to 18 years, and the requirements for a Risk Evaluation and Mitigation Strategy (REMS) to mitigate the risk of anaphylaxis had not been agreed upon. In addition, there were outstanding product quality related issues.
